title: Intelligent Vision Systems
text: Intelligent Vision Systems Welcome to the course website for Intelligent Vision Systems (Applied Computer Vision) , the 7th-semester vision course for BSES, Section A at the University of Lahore . This site is the main entry point for course information, lecture slides, the weekly schedule, lab handouts, and resources. The course follows a complete pipeline: from image formation and classical image processing, through features, geometry and motion, to deep learning and the deployment of real-time vision models on the Raspberry Pi 5 — optionally accelerated with the AI HAT / Hailo NPU and fed by a networked ESP32-CAM. Every one of the 16 weekly sessions pairs 1.5 hours of theory with 1.5 hours of supervised laboratory work, building toward a capstone vision system demonstrated live on target hardware.

title: Syllabus
text: Course Description Intelligent Vision Systems (Applied Computer Vision) is the capstone vision course for Embedded Systems students. It develops the complete machine-vision pipeline — from photons striking a sensor to a decision produced within the memory, power, and latency budget of a constrained device. The course begins with image formation and classical image processing, then moves through feature detection, multi-view geometry, and motion analysis, and finishes with modern deep-learning models for classification, detection, and segmentation. A recurring theme is deployment : taking an algorithm or a trained model and making it run in real time on the Raspberry Pi 5 , optionally accelerated with the AI HAT/Hailo NPU or fed by a networked ESP32-CAM. The course is project-driven: each 3-hour Monday session pairs 1.5 hours of theory with 1.5 hours of supervised laboratory work, and a capstone project asks every student to build and demonstrate a real-time vision application end-to-end on the Raspberry Pi 5. Learning Outcomes On successful completion, a student will be able to: CLO1. Explain the fundamentals of image formation, sensing, representation, colour, and processing. CLO2. Apply filtering, convolution, frequency-domain analysis, edge detection, and Hough methods. CLO3. Detect, describe, and match visual features and estimate geometric transforms robustly. CLO4. Apply camera geometry, calibration, stereo vision, and motion estimation for 3-D and dynamic scenes. CLO5. Implement classical recognition/detection (e.g. HOG, Haar, SIFT) and evaluate them. CLO6. Apply machine and deep learning to image classification, object detection, tracking, and segmentation. CLO7. Develop, deploy, and evaluate real-time computer-vision pipelines on embedded hardware (Raspberry Pi 5).

text: Assessment & Grading Each 3-hour Monday session pairs a 1.5-hour theory lecture with a 1.5-hour supervised laboratory on the Raspberry Pi 5. title: Syllabus
text: Course Policies Late Work Each student has a budget of 4 late days for the term, used in whole-day units, at most 2 per artefact. After the budget is spent, the maximum score drops 15% per day for up to 3 days, then reaches zero. Exams and the final presentation cannot use late days. Collaboration & Academic Integrity Discussing concepts is encouraged. The code and written answers you submit must be your own (or your team’s for the project). Cite any external code, dataset, or AI assistance you use. Copying solutions, sharing code between teams, or submitting generated text as your own analysis are integrity violations and are reported per university policy. AI Tools You may use AI assistants for debugging, boilerplate, and explanation. You may not use them to generate whole lab reports or exam answers. Add a one-line “AI use” note to each submission describing what you used them for. Attendance Lecture attendance is expected; labs are mandatory because equipment and check-offs happen in the room. Notify the instructor before a missed lab to arrange a make-up slot. Accommodations & Well-being Students with approved accommodations should share their letter in the first two weeks so arrangements can be made discreetly. If you are struggling, contact the instructor early — support is easier to arrange before a deadline than after.

title: Labs
text: Lab-by-lab Week Lab Title & objective Tasks Deliverable 1 Lab 1 Raspberry Pi 5 & Embedded Systems I — Setup. Flash Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit); headless SSH & VNC; system update & Python virtual environment; GPIO and basic embedded I/O; overview of embedded-vision constraints (compute, memory, power). A booted, updated Pi with a working OpenCV/Python environment + a short setup report. 2 Lab 2 Raspberry Pi 5 & Embedded Systems II — Camera, I/O & OpenCV 5.0. Install & verify OpenCV 5.0 (note key OpenCV 4→5 changes); connect and configure the Pi camera (libcamera/picamera2); read/write images and video on the Pi; remote development workflow; measure capture FPS and latency. A live capture application on OpenCV 5.0 + an FPS/latency note. 3 Lab 3 CV Fundamentals I — Images, Video & Drawing. Load and save images; load and save videos; drawing functions (lines, shapes, text); basic operations (resize, crop, rotate, ROI). An image/video I/O utility with on-frame annotations. 4 Lab 4 CV Fundamentals II — Colour, Arithmetic & Thresholding. Arithmetic and bitwise operations; masks; the HSV colour space and colour detection; global/Otsu/adaptive threshold operations. An HSV colour detector + a thresholding app. 5 Lab 5 CV Fundamentals III — Contours & Motion. Find and draw contours; contour features (area, perimeter, bounding boxes, polygon approximation); background subtraction and frame differencing. A contour-based object counter + a motion detector. 6 Lab 6 Filtering, Edges & Morphology. Smoothing and sharpening filters; Sobel and Canny edges; morphological operations (open/close); histogram equalisation & CLAHE — all on live Pi video. A tunable, real-time processing pipeline. 7 Lab 7 Features & Matching. Harris/Shi–Tomasi corners; ORB/SIFT descriptors; brute-force & FLANN matching; Hough lines and circles. A feature-matching + shape-detection application. 8 Lab 8 Geometry — Homography, Panorama & Calibration. Estimate a homography with RANSAC; stitch a panorama; calibrate the Pi camera and undistort frames. A stitched panorama + a saved camera-intrinsics file. 9 Lab 9 Build a Real-World CV System. Plan the project and design its architecture; measure the size of an object in 2-D (using calibration); build a defect-recognition system; integrate a database (SQLite/MySQL) to log results. An end-to-end measuring / defect system logging to a database. 10 Lab 10 Stereo & Depth. Stereo calibration; disparity via block-matching/SGBM; build a depth map; (optional) monocular depth estimation. A depth/disparity map on a real scene. 11 Lab 11 Tracking & Analytics. Optical flow / KLT; tracking-by-detection with OC-SORT and Strong-SORT; object trajectory; speed estimation; people/vehicle line-crossing counting. A tracking + counting + speed application. 12 Lab 12 Deep Learning — Classification & YOLO Detection. Classify images with a pretrained model and train a custom classifier by transfer learning (Colab, free GPU); then detect objects on image/video/camera with YOLO, train a custom detector, and try SAHI (small objects) and pose. A trained custom classifier + a custom YOLO detector running on the Pi. 13 Lab 13 Paper Implementation I — U-Net from Scratch. Read “U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation” (Ronneberger et al., 2015); understand the contracting/expanding paths and skip connections; implement the full architecture from scratch in PyTorch; train on a small segmentation dataset; evaluate with IoU/Dice and compare against a library U-Net. A from-scratch U-Net that segments a dataset + a one-page paper summary. 14 Lab 14 Modern Deployment with OpenCV 5.0 & Edge Runtimes. OpenCV 5.0 on the Pi: migrate an OpenCV 4 pipeline (deprecated APIs, moved modules), fix a CascadeClassifier call, and run YOLOv8n via ONNX in the new DNN engine with hardware acceleration. Then export to TFLite/ONNX, run on ONNX Runtime / Hailo, apply INT8 quantisation, and benchmark latency, throughput and power vs the CPU baseline. A migrated OpenCV 5 pipeline + YOLOv8n ONNX detection + a quantised model with a benchmark table. 15 Lab 15 Paper Implementation II — Transformer from Scratch. Read “Attention Is All You Need” (Vaswani et al., 2017); implement scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding and the encoder/decoder blocks from scratch in PyTorch; train on a toy sequence task; connect the mechanism to Vision Transformers (ViT). A working from-scratch Transformer + a paper summary bridging to ViT. 16 Capstone Deployed Vision System on the Raspberry Pi 5. Integrate the semester’s skills into one complete, real-time system deployed on the Pi; demonstrate live with a short talk, Q&A and peer review. Live capstone demo, assessed as the Lab Project (30 marks).

title: Labs
text: Capstone Project Students build one integrated, real-time vision system deployed on the Raspberry Pi 5 , demonstrated live with a short talk, Q&A and peer review. Assessed as the Lab Project (30 marks) — the largest single component of the course grade. Milestones When Milestone Deliverable Week 9 Project proposal Problem, target hardware tier, dataset/data plan, success metric. Week 15 Project report due Written report: method, architecture, on-device results, discussion. Week 16 Capstone demo Live demonstration on Raspberry Pi 5 target hardware + short talk + Q&A + peer review. Grading rubric (Lab Project = 30 of 100 course marks) Criterion Weight Technical difficulty & correctness 30% Runs on the Raspberry Pi 5 in real time (or a justified budget) 25% Experimental rigour — baselines, ablations, honest metrics 20% Report clarity & reproducibility 15% Presentation & demo 10% Advanced project bank Every project must run on the Raspberry Pi 5, include a simple GUI or dashboard, and log results. Projects are grouped by theme; each can be scaled up (edge deployment, multi-camera, alerting) for a higher grade. Detection, counting & monitoring: real-time object detection (YOLOv7/v8/v11/YOLO26) · weapon detection · people entry/exit counting (smart occupancy) · intrusion / zone monitoring · PPE-compliance detection · animal detection · vehicle traffic monitoring · smart parking (slot occupancy). Recognition & classification: face-recognition attendance system · facial-emotion detection · age & gender detection · traffic-sign recognition (EfficientNet) · face-mask detection · driver-distraction classification (ResNet-50). Tracking & analytics: vehicle speed tracking (calibrated) · licence-plate detection + recognition (OCR / VLM) · object trajectory & multi-object tracking (OC-SORT / Strong-SORT) · measure object size in 2-D. Pose, gesture & safety: driver-drowsiness detection (EAR/MAR) · human-fitness / exercise-rep tracking (pose) · fall-detection + alert · hand-gesture recognition & control. Systems & IoT integration: AI accident detection with MQTT alerting · defect-recognition with database logging · Flask/Tkinter dashboards · edge deployment with quantisation & benchmarking. Challenge tier (bonus): a custom visual-classification feature, video-based detection monitoring, or a full end-to-end custom vision system — designed with the instructor.
